```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, fig.align = "center",
                      dev = "png", dpi = 110)
```

## Overview

`bam2R_10x` returns one dense matrix per cell. That is convenient for a few
hundred cells, but a 10x Genomics experiment with thousands of cells needs
gigabytes of memory that way. `bam2R_v2` reads the same BAM file into
**sparse** matrices (sites x cells) and only stores what was actually
observed. In addition it

*   reads any number of regions on any chromosome in a single pass,
*   reports the forward and the reverse strand separately,
*   can count UMIs instead of reads (`umi.tag`),
*   can be restricted to the cells of interest (`barcodes`).

The result can be passed directly to `mutationCallsFromCohort`,
`mutationCallsFromExclusionlist` and `pullcountsVars`. This vignette walks
through that workflow and shows how to plot the results:

1.  read the counts,
2.  check the coverage,
3.  call patient specific variants with the cohort method, on the
    mitochondrial genome and on a nuclear target,
4.  check the variants for strand bias,
5.  look at the clones of a single patient.

```{r packages}
library(mitoClone2)
library(Matrix)
library(reshape2)
library(ggplot2)
library(viridis)
library(ComplexHeatmap)
```

## Reading the counts

The example BAM file of the package contains five cells of a mouse 10x
Genomics experiment.

```{r read}
bam <- system.file("extdata", "mm10_10x.bam", package = "mitoClone2")
example <- bam2R_v2(file = bam, sites = "chrM:1-15000")
#-- 16 matrices: 8 for the forward strand (capital letters), 8 for the reverse
names(example)
#-- covered sites x cells
dim(example$A)
example$A[c("chrM:13575", "chrM:13576", "chrM:13577"), ]
```

For a real experiment you would typically provide the barcodes of the cells
that passed the quality control, count UMIs instead of reads to remove PCR
duplicates and use several cores. The sites can be any set of regions:

```{r read_real, eval=FALSE}
#-- NOT RUN: a complete 10x Genomics experiment
barcodes <- read.table("filtered_feature_bc_matrix/barcodes.tsv.gz")$V1
counts <- bam2R_v2(file = "possorted_genome_bam.bam",
                   sites = c("chrM:1-16569", "chr7:140753000-140754000"),
                   barcodes = barcodes, umi.tag = "UB", ncores = 4)
```

For experiments with **one BAM file per cell** (e.g. Smart-seq2),
`baseCountsFromBamList_v2` returns the same sparse format, with one column
per file. Everything below works the same way for its output.

```{r read_bamlist, eval=FALSE}
#-- NOT RUN: one BAM file per cell, the names become the cell names
bamfiles <- c(cell1 = "cell1.bam", cell2 = "cell2.bam")
counts <- baseCountsFromBamList_v2(bamfiles, sites = "chrM:1-16569", ncores = 4)
```

## A larger example

Five cells are not enough to illustrate variant calling. For the remainder
of this vignette we therefore use **simulated** counts in exactly the format
that `bam2R_v2` returns: 360 cells from three patients, covering the human
mitochondrial genome and a 300 bp target on a toy chromosome 7. The
simulation plants

*   homoplasmic variants that are private to each patient,
*   heteroplasmic variants that mark clones and subclones within a patient,
*   a somatic and a germline heterozygous variant on chromosome 7,
*   variants that are shared by all cells of all patients (e.g. RNA editing),
*   an artifact that is only seen on one strand.

The code of the simulation is part of the source of this vignette.

```{r simulate, echo=FALSE}
simulateCounts <- function(n.cells = 120, seed = 42) {
    set.seed(seed)
    nts <- c("A", "T", "C", "G")
    ## reference: the human mitochondrial genome and a made up 300 bp target on chr7
    mito.ref <- getFromNamespace("hg38.dna", "mitoClone2")
    chr7.ref <- sample(nts, 6000, replace = TRUE)
    site <- data.frame(chr = rep(c("chrM", "chr7"), c(length(mito.ref), 300)),
                       pos = c(seq_along(mito.ref), 5001:5300),
                       stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    site$ref <- c(mito.ref, chr7.ref[5001:5300])
    site <- site[site$ref != "N", ]
    n.sites <- nrow(site)
    patient <- rep(c("P1", "P2", "P3"), each = n.cells)
    cells <- paste0(patient, "_", vapply(seq_along(patient), function(i)
        paste(sample(nts, 12, replace = TRUE), collapse = ""), ""), "-1")
    ## coverage: a smooth profile along the genome x the sequencing depth of the cell
    profile <- ifelse(site$chr == "chrM",
                      pmax(30 + 16 * sin(site$pos / 900) + 10 * cos(site$pos / 210), 8), 16)
    depth <- matrix(rpois(n.sites * length(cells),
                          outer(profile, rlnorm(length(cells), 0, 0.3))), n.sites)
    fwd <- matrix(rbinom(length(depth), depth, rbeta(n.sites, 8, 8)), n.sites)
    rev <- depth - fwd
    ## the variants: who carries them and at which heteroplasmy
    group <- function(pt, from, to) which(patient == pt)[round(from * n.cells + 1):round(to * n.cells)]
    mito <- function(n) sample(which(site$chr == "chrM" & site$pos > 600 & site$pos < 16000), n)
    chr7 <- function(pos) which(site$chr == "chr7" & site$pos == pos)
    het <- function(a, b) function(n) rbeta(n, a, b)
    variants <- list(
        ## homoplasmic variants that are private to a patient
        list(mito(3), group("P1", 0, 1), het(80, 1)), list(mito(3), group("P2", 0, 1), het(80, 1)),
        list(mito(3), group("P3", 0, 1), het(80, 1)),
        ## clones: P1 has clone A with a subclone and clone B
        list(mito(2), group("P1", 0, .55), het(9, 5)), list(mito(1), group("P1", 0, .25), het(6, 6)),
        list(mito(2), group("P1", .65, .9), het(5, 6)), list(chr7(5120), group("P1", 0, .55), het(60, 60)),
        ## P2 has one clone, P3 two clones (one with a subclone)
        list(mito(2), group("P2", .3, .75), het(7, 5)),
        list(mito(2), group("P3", 0, .4), het(8, 6)), list(mito(2), group("P3", .5, .85), het(6, 5)),
        list(mito(1), group("P3", .5, .7), het(5, 7)), list(chr7(5210), group("P3", 0, 1), het(60, 60)),
        ## present in every cell of every patient (e.g. RNA editing, common haplogroup)
        list(mito(5), seq_along(cells), het(3, 9)), list(mito(2), seq_along(cells), het(80, 1)),
        ## an artifact that only shows up on the forward strand
        list(mito(2), group("P2", 0, 1), het(4, 9), "forward"))
    alt.fwd <- alt.rev <- list()
    for (v in variants) for (s in v[[1]]) {
        af <- v[[3]](length(v[[2]]))
        ## transitions (A<>G, C<>T) are the most common mitochondrial variants
        alt <- c(A = "G", G = "A", C = "T", T = "C")[[site$ref[s]]]
        a.f <- rbinom(length(af), fwd[s, v[[2]]], af)
        a.r <- if (length(v) == 4) 0L else rbinom(length(af), rev[s, v[[2]]], af)
        fwd[s, v[[2]]] <- fwd[s, v[[2]]] - a.f
        rev[s, v[[2]]] <- rev[s, v[[2]]] - a.r
        alt.fwd[[length(alt.fwd) + 1]] <- data.frame(i = s, j = v[[2]], nt = alt, x = a.f)
        alt.rev[[length(alt.rev) + 1]] <- data.frame(i = s, j = v[[2]], nt = alt, x = a.r)
    }
    ## sequencing errors: 0.2 % of the reads show a random other nucleotide
    errors <- function(m) {
        e <- which(m > 0 & runif(length(m)) < 1 - (1 - 0.002)^m)
        data.frame(i = row(m)[e], j = col(m)[e], x = 1,
                   nt = nts[(match(site$ref[row(m)[e]], nts) + sample(3, length(e), TRUE) - 1) %% 4 + 1])
    }
    ## assemble the 16 sparse matrices in the format of bam2R_v2
    assemble <- function(m, alt) {
        alt <- rbind(do.call(rbind, alt), errors(m))
        alt <- alt[alt$x > 0, ]
        out <- lapply(nts, function(nt) {
            is.ref <- which(site$ref == nt)
            r <- which(m[is.ref, , drop = FALSE] > 0, arr.ind = TRUE)
            a <- alt[alt$nt == nt, ]
            Matrix::sparseMatrix(i = c(is.ref[r[, 1]], a$i), j = c(r[, 2], a$j),
                                 x = as.numeric(c(m[is.ref, , drop = FALSE][r], a$x)),
                                 dims = dim(m))
        })
        c(out, replicate(4, Matrix::sparseMatrix(i = integer(0), j = integer(0), x = numeric(0),
                                                 dims = dim(m))))
    }
    counts <- c(assemble(fwd, alt.fwd), assemble(rev, alt.rev))
    names(counts) <- c("A", "T", "C", "G", "-", "N", "INS", "DEL",
                       "a", "t", "c", "g", "_", "n", "ins", "del")
    counts <- lapply(counts, function(m) {
        dimnames(m) <- list(paste0(site$chr, ":", site$pos), cells)
        m
    })
    ## the toy genome as a FASTA file
    fasta <- file.path(tempdir(), "toy_genome.fa")
    writeLines(c(">chr7", paste(chr7.ref, collapse = "")), fasta)
    list(counts = counts, patient = patient, fasta = fasta)
}
```

```{r data}
sim <- simulateCounts()
counts <- sim$counts
patient <- sim$patient
#-- sites x cells
dim(counts$A)
table(patient)
```

Colors for the patients, used in all plots below.

```{r colors}
pts.colors <- c(P1 = "#FF7F00", P2 = "dodgerblue2", P3 = "#6A3D9A")
```

## Coverage

Every count matrix has one row per site, so the coverage along the genome is
a matter of summing the four nucleotides of both strands.

```{r coverage, fig.width=8, fig.height=3.2}
#-- reads per site and cell, both strands
depth <- Reduce("+", counts[c("A", "T", "C", "G", "a", "t", "c", "g")])
depth <- depth[grep("^chrM:", rownames(depth)), ]
#-- mean coverage per patient
cov.df <- melt(sapply(split(seq_along(patient), patient), function(cells) {
    Matrix::rowMeans(depth[, cells])
}))
colnames(cov.df) <- c("site", "Patient", "coverage")
cov.df$pos <- as.integer(gsub(".*:", "", cov.df$site))

ggplot(cov.df, aes(x = pos, y = coverage, color = Patient)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.4) + theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = pts.colors) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 5, color = "grey", linetype = "dashed") +
    xlab("Position on chrM") + ylab("Mean reads\nper cell")
```

## Calling variants across patients

The cohort method compares the patients with each other: a variant that is
found in the cells of a single patient is kept, a variant that is found in
several patients ends up on the exclusionlist. The sparse counts are passed
directly, the `sites` do not have to be specified.

By default only the mitochondrial chromosome is used. With
`all.chromosomes = TRUE` variants are called on every site of the counts.
The reference alleles of the other chromosomes are taken from the genome the
BAM file was aligned to, provided either as a FASTA file or as a BSgenome
object (e.g. `BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38::Hsapiens`). Here it is the FASTA
file of our toy genome. Without a reference the most abundant nucleotide of
a site is used as the reference allele, which is accompanied by a warning,
because homozygous variants can not be detected that way.

```{r cohort}
calls <- mutationCallsFromCohort(counts, patient = patient,
                                 all.chromosomes = TRUE, reference = sim$fasta)
#-- variants shared between patients
vars.exclusions <- calls[["exclusionlist"]]
vars.exclusions
calls[["exclusionlist"]] <- NULL
#-- one mutationCalls object per patient: cells x variants
sapply(calls, function(x) dim(x@M))
```

The names of the variants were made syntactically valid by R. A small helper
converts them back: `X1337G.A` (or `X1337.G.A`) to `1337G>A` and
`chr7.5120C.T` to `chr7:5120C>T`.

```{r helper}
fixvarName <- function(x) {
    x <- sub("^X(?=[0-9])", "", x, perl = TRUE)
    x <- sub("\\.?([ACGT])\\.([ACGT])$", "\\1>\\2", x)
    sub("^(.+)\\.([0-9]+[ACGT]>[ACGT])$", "\\1:\\2", x)
}
candidates <- lapply(calls, function(x) fixvarName(names(x@cluster)))
candidates
```

## Allele frequencies of the patient specific variants

`pullcountsVars` extracts the counts of the variant allele (M) and of all
other alleles (N) of any variant, in all cells.

```{r pull}
vars <- unlist(candidates, use.names = FALSE)
vars.patient <- rep(names(candidates), lengths(candidates))
MN <- pullcountsVars(counts, vars)
plotData <- MN$M / (MN$M + MN$N)
dim(plotData)
```

```{r heatmap, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=6}
#-- annotation of the cells (columns) and of the variants (rows)
ha_column <- HeatmapAnnotation(Patient = patient, col = list(Patient = pts.colors),
                               show_annotation_name = FALSE)
ha_row <- rowAnnotation(
    Chromosome = ifelse(grepl(":", vars), "chr7", "chrM"),
    col = list(Chromosome = c(chrM = "grey75", chr7 = "black")),
    show_annotation_name = FALSE)
Heatmap(plotData, col = viridis(100, option = "plasma"), na_col = "grey90",
        top_annotation = ha_column, left_annotation = ha_row,
        column_split = patient, row_split = vars.patient,
        cluster_row_slices = FALSE, cluster_column_slices = FALSE,
        show_column_names = FALSE, show_column_dend = FALSE, show_row_dend = FALSE,
        row_title = NULL, column_title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 18),
        row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 8), name = "Allele\nfreq.",
        use_raster = TRUE)
```

Each patient has a set of variants that is present in all of its cells and
further variants that are restricted to a part of the cells: the clones. The
two variants on chromosome 7 behave like the mitochondrial ones, at an allele
frequency around 0.5 as expected for heterozygous variants.

## Strand bias

True variants are seen on both strands. `strandBias10x` tabulates the reads of
the reference and alternate allele per strand and tests whether they are
distributed differently.

```{r strand}
strand <- strandBias10x(counts, vars)
#-- reads per allele and strand, strand odds ratio and the flag
show <- c("ref.fwd", "ref.rev", "alt.fwd", "alt.rev", "sor", "strand.flag")
head(strand[, show], 4)
strand[strand$strand.flag, show]
```

```{r strand_plot, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=4.6}
#-- allele frequency on each strand, in the cells of the patient with the variant
strand.df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(candidates), function(pt) {
    sb <- strandBias10x(counts, candidates[[pt]], cells = colnames(counts$A)[patient == pt])
    data.frame(var = rownames(sb), Patient = pt, flag = sb$strand.flag,
               Forward = sb$alt.fwd / (sb$alt.fwd + sb$ref.fwd),
               Reverse = sb$alt.rev / (sb$alt.rev + sb$ref.rev))
}))
cor_strand <- cor.test(strand.df$Forward[!strand.df$flag], strand.df$Reverse[!strand.df$flag])

ggplot(strand.df, aes(x = Forward, y = Reverse, color = Patient)) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, color = "grey", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_point(size = 4, alpha = 0.85) +
    geom_point(data = subset(strand.df, flag), shape = 21, size = 8,
               color = "red", stroke = 1) +
    annotate("text", x = 0.36, y = 0.08, hjust = 0, color = "red", size = 3.5,
             label = paste(c("forward strand only:", strand.df$var[strand.df$flag]),
                           collapse = "\n")) +
    annotate("text", x = 0.22, y = 0.92,
             label = sprintf("r = %.3f", cor_strand$estimate)) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 14) + scale_colour_manual(values = pts.colors) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
    xlab("Forward strand\nAllele frequency") + ylab("Reverse strand\nAllele frequency")
```

The allele frequencies of the two strands agree, except for the two flagged
variants (red circles) that are only supported by the forward strand. They
are the planted artifacts and are removed.

```{r strand_filter}
keep <- !strand$strand.flag
vars <- vars[keep]
vars.patient <- vars.patient[keep]
plotData <- plotData[keep, ]
candidates <- split(vars, vars.patient)
```

## Do the variants separate the patients?

The distance between the cells, based on the allele frequencies of the
remaining variants.

```{r distance, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=5.2}
#-- cells without coverage of a variant are ignored for that variant
distmat <- as.matrix(dist(t(plotData)))
ha_column <- HeatmapAnnotation(Patient = patient, col = list(Patient = pts.colors))
Heatmap(distmat, col = viridis(100), show_row_names = FALSE, show_column_names = FALSE,
        top_annotation = ha_column, show_column_dend = FALSE, show_row_dend = FALSE,
        name = "Euclidean\ndistance", use_raster = TRUE)
```

## The clones of a single patient

Zooming in on patient P1: next to the variants that all of its cells share
there are variants that are only found in a part of the cells.

```{r clones, fig.width=8, fig.height=3.6}
p1 <- plotData[candidates[["P1"]], patient == "P1"]
#-- group the cells by their variants
clone <- cutree(hclust(dist(t(p1 > 0.1), method = "binary"), method = "average"), k = 4)
clone.colors <- structure(c("#1B9E77", "#E7298A", "#E6AB02", "grey60"),
                          names = as.character(1:4))
ha_column <- HeatmapAnnotation(Clone = as.character(clone), col = list(Clone = clone.colors))
Heatmap(p1, col = viridis(100, option = "plasma"), na_col = "grey90",
        top_annotation = ha_column, column_split = clone,
        show_column_names = FALSE, show_column_dend = FALSE, show_row_dend = FALSE,
        column_title = NULL, row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 10),
        name = "Allele\nfreq.", use_raster = TRUE)
```

The mean allele frequency of every variant per clone summarizes the
structure: a variant close to 1 everywhere is a germline or early variant, a
variant restricted to some clones occurred later.

```{r clones_dot, fig.width=6.2, fig.height=3.6}
clone.df <- melt(sapply(split(seq_along(clone), clone), function(cells) {
    rowMeans(p1[, cells, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
}))
colnames(clone.df) <- c("var", "Clone", "af")
clone.df$cells <- as.vector(table(clone)[as.character(clone.df$Clone)])
ggplot(clone.df, aes(x = factor(Clone), y = var, color = af, size = cells)) +
    geom_point() + theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
    scale_color_viridis(option = "plasma", limits = c(0, 1), name = "Allele\nfreq.") +
    scale_size(range = c(3, 9), name = "Cells") +
    xlab("Clone") + ylab(NULL)
```

The location of the mitochondrial variants of the patient on the circular
genome is shown by `mitoPlot`. It expects the variants in the format
`1337 G>A`.

```{r mitoplot, fig.width=7, fig.height=7}
p1.mito <- grep(":", candidates[["P1"]], invert = TRUE, value = TRUE)
mitoPlot(sub("([ACGT]>[ACGT])$", " \\1", p1.mito))
```

The `mutationCalls` object of the patient can be passed on to `varCluster`
to infer a clonal hierarchy, as described in the *clustering* vignette.

## A single sample: the exclusionlist method

If there is only one sample, there is nothing to compare it to. In that case
`mutationCallsFromExclusionlist` removes variants on predefined
exclusionlists (RNA editing sites, homopolymers and recurrent artifacts). It
accepts the sparse counts as well and uses their mitochondrial chromosome.
Here we apply it to the cells of patient P1.

```{r exclusionlist}
counts.p1 <- lapply(counts, function(x) x[, patient == "P1"])
calls.p1 <- mutationCallsFromExclusionlist(counts.p1, min.af = 0.1, min.num.samples = 10)
from.exclusionlist <- fixvarName(names(calls.p1@cluster))
#-- variants of the cohort method that are found again
table(found = p1.mito %in% from.exclusionlist)
#-- variants that are only reported by the exclusionlist method
setdiff(from.exclusionlist, p1.mito)
```

Two differences are worth noting. The variants that are present in all cells
of the patient are missing: within a single sample they look like germline
variants and are removed (`universal.var.cells`), which is fine because they
do not distinguish any clones. The variants that are reported in addition are
the ones that are shared by all patients. Without the other patients they can
not be recognized as such, unless they are located on one of the
exclusionlists. We therefore recommend the cohort method whenever several
samples are available.
